coverage: All fifteen scenes: principal cast, differentiated civic and military speaking roles, family recollections, reported people and named allusions.

entities.name: Othello
entities.body: The general serving Venice, Desdemona’s husband and the play’s central figure.

entities.name: Desdemona
entities.body: Brabantio’s daughter and Othello’s wife.

entities.name: Iago
entities.body: Othello’s ensign and Emilia’s husband.

snapshots.body: Emilia’s husband, promoted by Othello from ensign to lieutenant.

entities.name: Emilia
entities.body: Iago’s wife and Desdemona’s attendant.

entities.name: Michael Cassio
entities.body: The Florentine officer chosen as Othello’s lieutenant.

snapshots.body: The Florentine officer dismissed from Othello’s lieutenancy.
The Florentine officer appointed to succeed Othello in governing Cyprus.

entities.name: Roderigo
entities.body: The Venetian gentleman pursuing Desdemona with Iago’s help.

entities.name: Brabantio
entities.body: Desdemona’s father, a Venetian senator.

entities.name: Bianca
entities.body: Cassio’s lover in Cyprus.

entities.name: Montano
entities.body: The governor of Cyprus whom Othello is sent to replace.

entities.name: Lodovico
entities.body: Desdemona’s kinsman, the envoy who comes from Venice.

entities.name: Gratiano
entities.body: Brabantio’s brother and Desdemona’s uncle.

entities.name: The Duke of Venice
entities.body: The ruler of Venice, presiding over the council.

entities.name: The first senator
entities.body: One of the Venetian senators discussing the military threat.

entities.name: The second senator
entities.body: Another senator comparing reports about the enemy fleet.

entities.name: The sailor
entities.body: The sailor bringing Angelo’s report to the Venetian council.

entities.name: The council messenger
entities.body: The messenger bringing Montano’s report to the Venetian council.

entities.name: The Cyprus messenger
entities.body: The messenger reporting the crowd’s sighting of a sail off Cyprus.

entities.name: The first gentleman
entities.body: One of Montano’s companions watching the sea from Cyprus.

entities.name: The second gentleman
entities.body: The gentleman helping identify the ships arriving at Cyprus.

entities.name: The third gentleman
entities.body: The gentleman bringing news of the fleet to Montano in Cyprus.

entities.name: Othello’s herald
entities.body: The official who publicly reads Othello’s proclamation.

entities.name: The Clown
entities.body: Othello’s household servant, who jokes with the musicians and carries messages.

entities.name: The first musician
entities.body: The musician answering the Clown outside Othello’s residence.

entities.name: The musicians
entities.body: The players Cassio brings to perform outside Othello’s residence.

entities.name: The wine-serving servant
entities.body: The attendant bringing wine to the officers’ gathering.

entities.name: The Venetian senators
entities.body: The council members overseeing Venice’s public and military affairs.

entities.name: The officers
entities.body: The military and civic officers attending the leading characters.

entities.name: The gondolier
entities.body: The boatman mentioned in Roderigo’s account of Desdemona’s departure.

entities.name: Signior Angelo
entities.body: The official whose naval report the sailor brings to Venice.

entities.name: Marcus Luccicos
entities.body: The man the duke asks for during the council’s discussion of Cyprus.

entities.name: Iago’s patrons
entities.body: The three influential Venetians whom Iago says supported his request for promotion.

entities.name: Othello’s mother
entities.body: The mother recalled in Othello’s account of the handkerchief.

entities.name: Othello’s father
entities.body: The father recalled in Othello’s account of the handkerchief.

entities.name: The Egyptian woman
entities.body: The woman who, in Othello’s account, gave his mother the handkerchief and described its powers.

entities.name: The sibyl
entities.body: The prophetess said by Othello to have sewn the handkerchief.

entities.name: Desdemona’s mother
entities.body: Brabantio’s wife, recalled in Desdemona’s story about her maid.

entities.name: Barbary
entities.body: Desdemona’s mother’s maid, remembered for her willow song.

entities.name: Barbary’s lover
entities.body: The man recalled in Desdemona’s account of Barbary.

entities.name: The Anthropophagi
entities.body: The man-eating people in Othello’s traveler’s tales.

entities.name: The men with heads beneath their shoulders
entities.body: The marvelous people described in Othello’s traveler’s tales.

entities.name: The Ottoman forces
entities.body: The forces threatening Venice’s possessions in the eastern Mediterranean.

entities.name: The man in Aleppo
entities.body: The Turkish man in Othello’s account of an incident in Aleppo.

entities.name: The Venetian in Aleppo
entities.body: The Venetian whom Othello recalls seeing attacked in Aleppo.

entities.name: The Judean in the comparison
entities.body: The figure in Othello’s comparison about throwing away a precious pearl; the precise identity is disputed.

entities.name: Janus
entities.body: The Roman god associated with beginnings and doorways, traditionally shown with two faces.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The Roman god of love.

entities.name: Jove
entities.body: Jupiter, the Roman king of the gods.

entities.name: King Stephen
entities.body: The English king in Iago’s drinking song.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman commander used as a comparison for military ability.

entities.name: The Hydra
entities.body: The many-headed monster of Greek myth.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The goddess associated with chastity, invoked here as Dian.

entities.name: Saint Peter
entities.body: The apostle traditionally associated with the keys of heaven.

entities.name: Prometheus
entities.body: The mythical bringer of fire, invoked in Othello’s image of life-giving heat.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The deity invoked in the play’s prayers and exclamations.

entities.name: The devil
entities.body: The supernatural figure invoked in curses and accusations.
